- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or volatile (alternating ±0.5+), model often overcorrects or lags — increase forecast slope or add 0.5–1.5 price point buffer to avoid undershoot.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2 price points below peak or apply exponential decay to momentum.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–75), model often fails to recognize — reduce forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0 price point downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates upward moves in bullish sentiment windows — apply sentiment-weighted upward bias (e.g., +0.3–0.7x sentiment score × price range).
- If sentiment history shows sudden reversal (e.g., 0.00 → 1.00 or vice versa), model often misreads direction — add 0.5–1.0 price point lag correction or use 2-day moving average to smooth transition.
